## Epigenetic Clos 

- [Biolearn](https://bio-learn.github.io/clocks.html)

### First Generation  

Primarily estimate biological age based on DNA methylation patterns, aiming to predict chronological age

- [Horvath 1](https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/gb-2013-14-10-r115): pan-tissue Horvath clock (353-CpG clock) using 8,000 samples encompassing 51 different tissueand cell types
- [Horvathv 2](https://www.aging-us.com/article/101508/text): we developed a novel and highly robust DNAm age estimator (based on 391 CpGs) for human fibroblasts, keratinocytes, buccal cells, endothelial cells, lymphoblastoid cells, skin, blood, and saliva samples
- [Hannum](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1097276512008933): 71- CpG clock using 656 whole-blood samples
- [PedBE](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1820843116): 94 CpG clock using 1,721 pediatric (0-20y) buccal epithelial cell samples
- [Lin](https://www.aging-us.com/article/100908/text): 99 CpG clock predicting age using Lothian Birth Cohort

### Second Generation 

Second-generation clocks are designed to predict health outcomes, morbidity, and mortality more accurately, often incorporating additional clinical or phenotypic data alongside DNA methylation patterns.

- [Zhang](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms14617): 10 CpG clock for mortality risk
- [PhenoAge](): uses standard methods butpredicts a composite biological age score 31 based on alinear combination of chronological age and nine clini-cal parameters associated with mortality risk.
- [GrimAge1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6366976/): Seven DNAm-based estimators of plasma proteins including those of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) and growth differentiation factor 15. The resulting predictor of lifespan, DNAm GrimAge (in units of years), is a composite biomarker based on the seven DNAm surrogates and a DNAm-based estimator of smoking pack-years. Adjusting DNAm **GrimAge** for chronological age generated novel measure of epigenetic age acceleration, **AgeAccelGrim**.
- [GrimAge2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9792204/): Here we describe version 2 of GrimAge (trained on individuals aged between 40 and 92) which leverages two new DNAm based estimators of (log transformed) plasma proteins: high sensitivity C-reactive protein (logCRP) and hemoglobin A1C (logA1C). 13,399 blood samples across nine study cohorts.

### Third Generation

- [DunedinPoAm38](https://elifesciences.org/articles/54870): Dunedin Study members for whom age-38 DNA methylation data were available (N = 810). We applied elastic-net regression (Zou and Hastie, 2005) using Pace of Aging between ages 26 to 38 years as the criterion.
- [DunedinPACE](https://elifesciences.org/articles/73420): Improved over PoAM38, longer follow-up, more time points. 
- [CausAge](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43587-023-00557-0): epigenome-wide Mendelian randomization, we identified CpG sites potentially causal for aging-related traits. We established a new framework to introduce causal information into epigenetic clocks, resulting in **DamAge** and **AdaptAge**—clocks that track detrimental and adaptive methylation changes, respectively. DamAge correlates with adverse outcomes, including mortality, while AdaptAge is associated with beneficial adaptations.    

## ADNI


```{r}
## Clinical
merge.raw <- read_csv("resources/ADNI/ADNIMERGE_25Sep2023.csv")

merge <- select(merge.raw, RID, PTID, COLPROT, ORIGPROT, VISCODE, EXAMDATE, EXAMDATE_bl, AGE, PTGENDER, PTEDUCAT, APOE4, 
                DX_bl, DX, CDRSB, ADAS13,
                FDG, PIB, AV45, FBB, ABETA, TAU, PTAU, ADAS13, Hippocampus, WholeBrain) %>%
  arrange(RID, EXAMDATE) %>%
  group_by(RID) %>%
  mutate(
    years_since_baseline = as.numeric(difftime(EXAMDATE, EXAMDATE_bl, units = "days")) / 365.25,
    age = AGE + years_since_baseline
  )
  
merge %>%
  group_by(merge.raw, RID, PTID, COLPROT, ORIGPROT, VISCODE, EXAMDATE, DX_bl, CDRSB, AGE, APOE4, DX)
```


A total of 649 ADNI participants hadmethylation data. Participants varied on the number of repeatDNA methylation measurements they had: 83 had only abaseline measurement; 121 had 2 measurements (baseline plus 1repeat), mean 14.5 months between measurements (SD = 7.06);407 had 3 measurements, mean 12.1 months between mea-surements (SD = 1.5); 29 had 4, mean 10.4 months betweenmeasurements (SD = 3.54); and 9 had 5, mean 12.5 monthsbetween measurements (SD = 2.25). [Sugden et al 2022](https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000200898)


```{r}
## Mythylation
map.raw <- readxl::read_xlsx("resources/ADNI/ADNI_DNA_Methylation_SampleAnnotation_20170530.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(Edate = as.Date(Edate))
clocks.raw <- read_csv("intermediate/adni_epiclocks_240826.csv") %>%
  rename(barcodes = '...1' ) 

dnam.raw <- map.raw %>%
  select(barcodes, RID, Phase,  Edate, DateDrawn, PlateNumber, Array) %>%
  rename(Phase_methy = Phase,  Edate_methy = Edate, DateDrawn_methy = DateDrawn) %>%
  arrange(RID, Edate_methy, PlateNumber) %>%
  left_join(clocks.raw, by = 'barcodes') 

dnam <- dnam.raw %>% 
  group_by(RID, Edate_methy) %>%
  distinct(RID, .keep_all = T) %>%
  group_by(RID) %>%
  slice(1:3)%>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-Age)

```

```{r}
## Genetics 
gen.raw <- read_csv("resources/ADNI/APOE_GENETIC_27Aug2024.csv") %>%
  arrange(RID, VISDATE) 

apoe_wgs.path <- "resources/ADNI/ADNI.808_indiv.minGQ_21.pass.ADNI_ID.chr19.vcf/apoe_region.vcf"

apoe_wgs <- vcfR::vcfR2tidy(vcf_data, format_fields = c("GT")) %>%
  magrittr::extract2('gt') %>%
  filter(POS %in% c("45411941", "45412079")) %>%
  select(-ChromKey, -gt_GT) %>%
  mutate(
    POS = ifelse(POS == 45412079, 'rs7412', 'rs429358'), 
    RID = sub("^0+", "", str_extract(Indiv, "\\d{4}$")), 
    RID = as.numeric(RID)
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = POS, values_from = gt_GT_alleles) %>%
  arrange(RID)
  

semi_join(gen.raw, apoe_wgs, by = c('PTID' = 'Indiv')) 
semi_join(gen.raw, apoe_wgs, by = c('PTID' = 'Indiv')) %>%
  group_by(PTID) %>% slice_max(VISDATE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  count(PHASE, VISCODE2)
```


```{r}

rids <- bind_rows(
  select(ts, RID), 
  select(dnam, RID)
) %>%
  distinct(RID)


adni.raw <- merge %>%
  left_join(select(apoe_wgs, -RID), by = c("PTID" = "Indiv")) %>%
  left_join(dnam %>% select(-DateDrawn_methy, -Phase_methy),
            by = c('RID', 'EXAMDATE' = 'Edate_methy')) %>%
  left_join(ts %>% select(-VISCODE, -VISCODE2, -update_stamp, -DATE_DRAWN, -DATE_RECEIVED, -PHASE), 
            by = c('RID', 'EXAMDATE' = 'EXAM_DATE')) %>%
  semi_join(rids) %>%
  mutate(
        months = case_when(
      VISCODE == "bl" ~ '0', 
      str_detect(VISCODE, "m*") ~ str_replace(VISCODE, "m", "")
    ), 
    months = as.numeric(months), 
  ) %>%
  relocate(months, .after = VISCODE)
  
adni <- adni.raw %>% 
  filter(!is.na(PlateNumber) | !is.na(PLATE)) %>%
  group_by(RID) %>%
  mutate(
    visit = 1:n(),
    visits = n()
  )  %>%
  relocate(visit, visits, .after = months) %>%
  ungroup()


adni %>% 
  # filter(visits == 3) %>%
  group_by(visit) %>%
  summarise(
    age = mean(age),
    n = n(),
    n_wgs = sum(!is.na(rs7412)),
    n_mth = sum(!is.na(CausAge)),
    n_tel = sum(!is.na(TS_RATIO))
  ) 

```

```{r}
ba <- dnam %>% 
  select(barcodes, RID, Edate_methy, AGE, DX, CDRSB, Horvathv2, Hannum, Lin, PhenoAge, CausAge, DNAmGrimAgev2) %>%
  group_by(RID) %>%
  slice_min(Edate_methy) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Horvathv2:DNAmGrimAgev2, 
    names_to = 'clock', 
    values_to = 'ba'
  )


ggplot(ba, aes(x = AGE, y = ba, colour = clock)) + 
  facet_wrap(facets = vars(clock)) + 
  geom_point(color = 'black') + 
  geom_smooth(method='lm', formula= y~x) + 
  theme_bw()
  
ggplot(ba, aes(x = AGE, y = ba, colour = DX)) + 
  facet_wrap(facets = vars(clock)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method='lm', formula= y~x, color = "black") + 
  theme_bw()
  

ggplot(ba, aes(x = CDRSB, y = ba, colour = clock)) + 
  facet_wrap(facets = vars(clock)) + 
  geom_point(color = 'black') + 
  geom_smooth(method='lm', formula= y~x) + 
  theme_bw()

```
